/-- **(C2) effectivity from a covering family of trivialized pieces** (arbitrary
faithfully flat cover): a class on the cover curve represented by `γ`, rigidified along
the base-changed section and with equal coprojection pullbacks on the nose, descends
along `cg` — provided every point of the base curve lies in an affine piece on which

theorem exists_cechPic_map_whiskerLeft_eq_of_pieces
    (𝒩 : (XB).PointedCover) (γ : (XB).unitsCocycle 𝒩)
    (hrig : Over.IsRigidified

20	sessions on this leaf priced it: on an **affine** test the canonical field point `Over.testPoint t`
21	**is** the base-change morphism `overSpecMap A κ(t)`.  Both sides are `Spec` of the same ring map —
22	`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine` is *defined* as `Spec.preimage` of `fromSpecResidueField`,
23	so `Spec.map_preimage` closes it — but nothing in the tree said so, and every plus-class identity

25	`relCurveMap`.  Without the comparison the two sides are not even syntactically comparable; with
26	it they are the same class.

29	
30	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D` compares `μ`'s fibre at `κ(t)`, read as a plus class, with the
31	plus-*unit* of `D`'s fibre class.  So the natural hypothesis on `μ` is that it is *already* a
32	plus unit — i.e. in the image of the sheafification unit `relPicToPicEt` — and then `D` comes

103	`Scheme.fromSpecResidueField`, while `overSpecMap A κ(t)` is `Spec` of `algebraMap A κ(t)`.  They
104	are equal because the `A`-algebra structure on `κ(t)` (`instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) is
105	*defined* to be `Spec.preimage` of that very morphism, so `Spec.map_preimage` is the whole proof.
106	
107	**Why this was the gate.**  Every plus-class identity on this lane compares a class pulled along
108	`Over.testPoint` (the `chartLocus` side, indexed by points of a test) with one pulled along
109	`relCurveMap C A κ(t)` (the datum side, indexed by base change).  Absent this lemma the two are
110	not syntactically comparable and no producer can be written; with it they are the same morphism
111	and the producer below is three rewrites.  The lemma is *cheap*, which is the point: four
112	sessions on this leaf priced the missing producer as the identification of a fibre class, i.e.
113	as geometry, when what was missing was a comparison of two spellings of one morphism. -/
114	theorem testPoint_eq_overSpecMap {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
115	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
116	    Over.testPoint t
117	      = overSpecMap (k := k) A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
118	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
119	  simp only [Over.testPoint_left, overSpecMap_left]
120	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
121	  exact (Spec.map_preimage _).symm

123	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

126	`relCurveMap`.  This is the shape `IsChartDatumPlusFibre` reads on its right-hand side. -/
127	theorem relCurveMap_testPoint {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
128	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
129	    (C ◁ Over.testPoint t).left
130	      = relCurveMap C A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) := by
131	  rw [testPoint_eq_overSpecMap]
132	  rfl

134	/-! ## The producer -/
135	
136	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
137	variable (C π) in
138	/-- **THE PRODUCER, with the datum supplied**: if `μ` is the unit image of a relative Picard
139	class presented by the Čech class `L₀`, then any datum whose class is `L₀` satisfies
140	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`.

142	The proof is four rewrites and no geometry.  `picEtMap_relPicToPicEt` moves the restriction to
143	`κ(t)` inside the unit; `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt` collapses the affine comparison to
144	`PicEtAff.unit`; `PicEtAff.map_id` deletes the identity restriction `κ(t) → κ(t)` that
145	`IsChartDatumPlusFibre`'s left-hand side carries; and `relCurveMap_testPoint` identifies

148	Note which hypotheses are absent: no witness, no `H¹`, no divisor, no degree, no separability,
149	and no certificate.  The plus-class identity was never geometry — it is the statement that the
150	two ways of restricting a *unit* to a residue field agree.
151	
152	**A measurement, not a claim, and it is independent evidence for that reading**: this theorem does
153	not use `GeometricallyReduced C.hom` either — the linter says so, hence the `omit`.  A statement
154	about a fibre class would need the curve's geometry; this one needs the curve only to have the
155	functor defined. -/
156	theorem isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
157	    (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k A).left.CechPic) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π)
158	    (hD : D.cechPicClass = L₀) :
159	    IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π
160	      (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) (relPicMk C (overSpec k A) L₀)) D := by
161	  intro t
162	  rw [picEtMap_relPicToPicEt, picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, PicEtAff.map_id, hD,
163	    relPicMap_mk, relCurveMap_testPoint]
164	  rfl
165	
166	omit [GeometricallyReduced C.hom] in
167	variable (C π) in
168	/-- **THE PRODUCER PROPER**: for a class in the image of the sheafification unit, a datum with
169	the plus-class property EXISTS.
170	
171	The datum comes from `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq` (the extraction keystone,
172	`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) applied to any Čech representative of the class, and
173	`relPicMk_surjective` supplies the representative.  So the existential
174	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` asks for is met outright, with no choice left to the caller.
175	
176	This is the statement `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusPlusFibre.lean`'s header names as not claimed, and it
177	too is `GeometricallyReduced`-free. -/
178	theorem exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A))
180	    (hμ : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k A), relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k A) z = μ) :
181	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π, IsChartDatumPlusFibre C π μ D := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := hμ
183	  obtain ⟨L₀, rfl⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k A) z
184	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq
185	    (C := C) (B := A) (π := π) L₀
186	  exact ⟨D, isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_relPicToPicEt C π L₀ D hD⟩

188	/-! ## The honesty hypothesis, and why it is not vacuous -/
189	
190	variable (C) in
191	/-- **The honesty hypothesis: `μ` is a plus unit on every affine piece of the test.**
192	
193	This is the one thing the producer needs of `μ`, and it is a genuine hypothesis rather than a
194	restatement: a plus class over `Spec A` is `PicEtAff.mk E x` for an étale cover `E`, and
195	`Picard/Pic0ChartHonest.lean` is the record that it becomes honest over `E.Carrier` and not over
196	`A`.  So `IsPlusHonest` is exactly the gap between an arbitrary class and one the producer reaches.
197	
198	It is stated per affine piece because that is the shape `isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` consumes;
199	over an affine test it is the single condition that `μ` is in the range of `relPicToPicEt`. -/
200	def IsPlusHonest (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (μ : picEt C T) : Prop :=
201	  ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens, ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)),
202	    relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1)) z
203	      = picEtMap C (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) μ

207	/-- Honesty is closed under multiplication — the range of `relPicToPicEt` is a subgroup, and
208	`picEtMap` is a homomorphism. -/
209	theorem IsPlusHonest.mul {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ ν : picEt C T}
210	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (hν : IsPlusHonest C T ν) :
211	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ * ν) := by
212	  intro U
213	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
214	  obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hν U
215	  exact ⟨z * w, by rw [map_mul, hz, hw, map_mul]⟩
216

218	variable (C) in
219	/-- Honesty is closed under inversion. -/
220	theorem IsPlusHonest.inv {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
221	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) :
222	    IsPlusHonest C T μ⁻¹ := by
223	  intro U
224	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
225	  exact ⟨z⁻¹, by rw [map_inv, hz, map_inv]⟩
226	
227	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] in
228	variable (C) in
229	/-- Honesty is closed under powers. -/
230	theorem IsPlusHonest.pow {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {μ : picEt C T}
231	    (hμ : IsPlusHonest C T μ) (m : ℕ) :
232	    IsPlusHonest C T (μ ^ m) := by
233	  intro U
234	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := hμ U
235	  exact ⟨z ^ m, by rw [map_pow, hz, map_pow]⟩
236	
237	variable (C) in
238	/-- **A θ-family is honest at every test** — the first half of the non-vacuity check.
239	
240	`thetaFamily_natural` restricts a θ-family to a θ-family, and `thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv`
241	says its affine collapse is the plus unit of the base-changed base class.  So a θ-family is in the
242	range of the unit on every affine piece, with no hypothesis on the curve.
243	
244	This is why `chartTwist` preserves honesty: two of its three factors are θ-families. -/
245	theorem thetaFamily_isPlusHonest (L₀ : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)
246	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
247	    IsPlusHonest C T (thetaFamily C L₀ T) := by
248	  intro U
249	  refine ⟨relPicAlgMap C (Algebra.ofId k Γ(T.left, U.1)) (relPicMk C (overSpec k k) L₀), ?_⟩
250	  rw [thetaFamily_natural]
251	  exact (picEtAffineEquiv C Γ(T.left, U.1)).injective (by
252	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt, thetaFamily_overSpec_affineEquiv])
253	
254	variable (C) in
255	/-- A Σ-family is honest: it *is* a θ-family (`sigmaFamily` is defined as one). -/
256	theorem sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
257	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
258	    IsPlusHonest C T (sigmaFamily C Z T) :=
259	  thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C _ T
260	
261	variable (C π) in
262	/-- **THE ABEL VALUE IS HONEST AT EVERY TEST** — the witness that carries weight, and the one this
263	file's header cited by name before it existed (see the header's own retraction).
264	
265	The θ- and Σ-family witnesses above are the *twist factors*, which `chartTwist_isPlusHonest`
266	discharges anyway; they say nothing about the class being charted.  Since
267	`chartValue = abelDiv · Σ · (θᵐ)⁻¹` and honesty is a subgroup condition, honesty of a **chart
268	value** reduces to honesty of `abelDiv` — so this is the row that makes CHART-U(b) unconditional
269	on the classes DAT-C's Σ-chart actually reads.
270	
271	It is cheap for a structural reason: `abelDiv`'s components are `abelDivPlus`, i.e. `PicEtAff.unit`
272	of `relPicMk` of the family's class, and `relPicToPicEt`'s components are `PicEtAff.unit` of
273	`relPicMap` — so the witness on the piece `U` is the class of the *restricted* family, and
274	`abelDiv_val` plus `picEtMap_abelDiv` line the two up. -/
275	theorem abelDiv_isPlusHonest {n : ℕ} (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
276	    (s : divFamZar C π n T) :
277	    IsPlusHonest C T (abelDiv C π n T s) := by
278	  intro U
279	  refine ⟨relPicMk C (overSpec k Γ(T.left, U.1))
280	    ((divFamZarAffineEquiv C π n Γ(T.left, U.1)
281	      (divFamZar.map C π n (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) s)).picClass), ?_⟩
282	  rw [picEtMap_abelDiv, abelDiv_overSpec]
283	  rfl
284	
285	variable (C) in
286	/-- **`chartTwist` PRESERVES honesty** — the reason the producer reaches the Σ-chart.
287	
288	`chartTwist λ = λ · θᵐ · Σ⁻¹`, and both twist factors are θ-families, hence honest at every test
289	with no hypothesis.  Since honesty is a subgroup condition, the twisted class is honest exactly
290	when `λ` is.
291	
292	So the residue of CHART-U(b) is **the λ-factor alone**: no twist bookkeeping enters, which is the
293	mis-pricing the §3.3 correction 5 records. -/
294	theorem chartTwist_isPlusHonest (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
295	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) {lam : picEt C T} (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
296	    IsPlusHonest C T (chartTwist C m Z T lam) := by
297	  rw [chartTwist]
298	  exact (hlam.mul C ((thetaFamily_isPlusHonest C (thetaCechClass C) T).pow C m)).mul C
299	    ((sigmaFamily_isPlusHonest C Z T).inv C)
300	
301	/-! ## CHART-U(b) with the residue discharged -/
302	
303	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
304	variable (C π) in
305	/-- **CHART-U(b) AT A GENERAL TEST, WITH NO RESIDUE**, for a class that is honest on the affine
306	pieces of the test.
307	
308	`isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre` needs a per-piece datum with the plus-class property;
309	`exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range` produces one from honesty, and
310	`chartTwist_isPlusHonest` says the twist does not disturb honesty.  So the whole chain — the
311	engine, RE-5, the dictionary, the fibre-field invariance, `haff`, the presentation, `hconv`,
312	`hplus`, and now the producer — closes on the single hypothesis `IsPlusHonest`.
313	
314	`IsAffineHom π` follows from `IsFinite π`, whence the disabled overlapping-instance linter — the
315	same configuration `chartLocusAffineLocal_of_plusFibre` carries and for the same reason. -/
316	theorem isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest
317	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
318	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
319	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
320	    IsOpen (chartLocus C m Z lam) :=
321	  isOpen_chartLocus_of_plusFibre C π hπ m Z T lam fun U =>
322	    exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range C π _
323	      (by
324	        obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := chartTwist_isPlusHonest C m Z T hlam U
325	        exact ⟨z, hz.trans (picEtMap_chartTwist m Z (Over.fromSpecAffine T U) lam)⟩)
326	
327	set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
328	variable (C π) in
329	/-- **The chart locus as an OPEN OF THE TEST, from honesty alone** — the shape the `W` field of a
330	chart datum consumes (`chartLocusOpens`, `Picard/Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:115`), with its `haff`
331	argument discharged rather than passed through.
332	
333	This is c9b's clause (i) paid in full for an honest class: not "reduced to", but produced. -/
334	def chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
335	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
336	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
337	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (lam : picEt C T) (hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam) :
338	    T.left.Opens where
339	  carrier := chartLocus C m Z lam
340	  is_open' := isOpen_chartLocus_of_isPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam
341	
342	@[simp]
343	lemma mem_chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest
344	    {hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom}
345	    {m : ℕ} {Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor}
346	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} {lam : picEt C T} {hlam : IsPlusHonest C T lam}

348	    t ∈ chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest C π hπ m Z T lam hlam ↔ t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam :=

open AlgebraicJacobian

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

noncomputable section

/-! ## Honesty over the cover's own carrier -/

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- **A plus class becomes the plus-unit of an honest class over its own cover carrier**, over
an ARBITRARY affine base `A` — no field, no finiteness, no separability.

`PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x) = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier x`: the class
presented by `x` on the cover `E` restricts, along `A → E.Carrier`, to the tautological plus
unit of `x` itself.

This is the general-base analogue of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_of_algHom`
(`Picard/PicEtAffFieldCollapse.lean:79`) at `ℓ := AlgHom.id`.  That lemma carries `[Field K]`,
`[Field L]` because *its* consumer (the degree seam) reads a degree; the argument itself uses
neither.  The substantive content, identical in both, is the **descent condition** `x.2`: the
two ways of carrying `x` into the base-changed carrier — along `E.baseChangeInclude` and along
`Algebra.ofId` — agree on a descent class, which is what `relPicAlgMap_congr` consumes.

Why this matters: the tree's only previous route from a plus class to an honest one was étale
field-cofinality (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`), which is field-only, so "honesty over a general
affine base" was recorded as an unlanded *construction*.  It is not a construction at all — a
cover splits over its own carrier, and the identity map is the splitting. -/
theorem PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (x : descentClasses C E) :
    PicEtAff.map C E.Carrier (PicEtAff.mk C E x)
      = PicEtAff.unit C E.Carrier (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
  rw [PicEtAff.map_mk, PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)]
  refine congrArg (PicEtAff.mk C (E.baseChange E.Carrier)) (Subtype.ext ?_)
  rw [descentBaseChange_coe]
  exact relPicAlgMap_congr C (E.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier)
    ((Algebra.ofId E.Carrier (E.baseChange E.Carrier).Carrier).restrictScalars A) x.2

omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
variable (C) in
/-- **Every plus class over an affine base is honest over some affine base above it** — the
existential form of `PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self`, which is how a consumer meets it: it does
not get to choose `B`, it gets a `B` from the class's own presentation.

Compare `exists_splitting_of_picEt` (`Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`): that gives a *field*
extension and requires the base to be a field; this gives an étale extension and requires
nothing.  The two are the field and general-base halves of the same move, and the chart layer
needs both — the field one to read the split witness predicate at a point, this one to run the
engine over a base. -/
theorem exists_honest_of_picEtAff {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    (a : PicEtAff C A) :
    ∃ (B : Type u) (_ : CommRing B) (_ : Algebra k B) (_ : Algebra A B)
        (_ : IsScalarTower k A B) (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)),
      PicEtAff.map C B a = PicEtAff.unit C B z := by
  induction a using PicEtAff.ind with
  | mk E x =>
    refine ⟨E.Carrier, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
      (x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)), ?_⟩
    exact PicEtAff.map_mk_eq_unit_self C E x

/-! ## The payoff: the engine's input, with honesty discharged -/

variable (C π) in
/-- **The engine input, assembled**: for any plus class over any affine base `A` and any chart
index `(m, Z)`, once the class is read honestly over a base `B` above `A` by a Čech class `c`,
a `BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `B` presenting `c` twisted by the chart index exists.

This composes the two halves that were previously recorded as separate gates:

* honesty over `B := E.Carrier` — `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` above, which needs no field;
* presentation of the twisted class by a datum — `exists_cechPicClass_eq`, applied at the
  *product* class, which is why no `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.mul` is needed
  (`Picard/Pic0ChartTwistCollapse.lean`).

The conclusion is exactly the input of
`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing`, so the openness of the witness
locus over `Spec B` is available for every plus class and every chart index.  What is *not* here
is the identification of that locus with `chartLocus` — that is `IsChartDatumPresentation`, the
one genuine remaining obligation of CHART-U(b).

Stated with `c` as a hypothesis rather than bundled into the existential: bundling it forces the
elaborator to unify the tower instances on `B` while `B` is still a metavariable, which is the
hazard recorded at `Picard/Pic0ChartSplit.lean`'s closing note.  A consumer obtains `B` and `c`
from `exists_honest_of_picEtAff` plus `relPicMk_surjective`, then applies this. -/
theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_twist {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (m : ℕ)
    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
      D.cechPicClass
        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
  exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass c m Z

end

end AlgebraicGeometry

9	/-!
10	# The étale plus construction of the relative Picard functor on affine tests
11	
12	For a curve `C` over `k` and an affine test scheme `Spec A`, the étale-sheafified relative
13	Picard group is computed by a *single* plus construction (the relative Picard presheaf is
14	étale-separated, by descent — proved separately): a class of the plus is represented by a
15	relative Picard class on an étale cover `Spec B → Spec A` equipped with a *descent
16	condition* — equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double cover
17	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B)` — and two representatives are identified when they agree on a common
18	refinement.
19	
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentClasses C E`: the subgroup of `relPic C (Spec B)` of classes
21	  satisfying the descent condition on the cover `E` with carrier `B`.
22	* `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap C h`: transport of descent classes along a refinement map
23	  `h` of covers.
24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPicAlgMap_congr` (**the keystone**): a descent class restricts
25	  equally along any two `A`-algebra maps out of the cover carrier — the pair `(j₁, j₂)`
26	  factors through the double cover, where the descent condition kills the difference.
27	  Specialized to refinement maps as `AlgebraicGeometry.descentMap_congr`, this is what
28	  makes the colimit below independent of all choices; applied across base rings
29	  (`Picard/PicEtAffMap.lean`), it is also what makes the plus functorial in the test
30	  algebra.
31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff C A`: the one-step plus — descent classes on some cover,
32	  modulo agreement on a common refinement — with its `CommGroup` structure and the
33	  constructor/eliminator API `PicEtAff.mk`, `PicEtAff.ind`, `PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff`,
34	  `PicEtAff.mk_descentMap`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.unit`: the unit `relPic C (Spec A) →* PicEtAff C A` of the
36	  plus construction — a class pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological
37	  descent datum.
38	
39	The functoriality of `PicEtAff` in `A` (restriction along test maps, via base change of
40	covers) and the comparison theorems (injectivity of the unit = separatedness; bijectivity
41	under a section = rigidification) are subsequent layers, consuming only this interface.
42	-/

61	/-- The first coprojection from the carrier of a cover into its self-tensor product over
62	the base — the algebra face of the first projection of the double cover
63	`Spec (B ⊗[A] B) → Spec B` — as a `k`-algebra map. -/
64	def doubleInl (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
65	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
66	  Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
67	
68	/-- The second coprojection into the self-tensor product; see `doubleInl`. -/
69	def doubleInr (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
70	    E.Carrier →ₐ[k] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
71	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight).restrictScalars k
72	
73	/-- The subgroup of relative Picard classes on an étale cover of the test algebra
74	satisfying the descent condition: equal pullbacks along the two projections of the double
75	cover. -/
76	def descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
77	    Subgroup (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
78	  MonoidHom.eqLocus
79	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E))
80	    (relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E))

82	lemma mem_descentClasses_iff {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
83	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} :
84	    x ∈ descentClasses C E ↔
85	      relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
86	        = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x :=
87	  Iff.rfl

91	private lemma doubleInl_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
92	    (doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
93	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) := by
94	  ext x
95	  simp [doubleInl]

97	private lemma doubleInr_comp {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
98	    (doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)
99	      = ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) := by
100	  ext x
101	  simp [doubleInr]

103	/-- The descent condition is natural in the cover: pullback along a refinement map sends
104	descent classes to descent classes. -/
105	lemma relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
106	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)}
107	    (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
108	    relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x ∈ descentClasses C F := by
109	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff] at hx ⊢
110	  calc relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x)
111	      = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInl F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x :=
112	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
113	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
114	          (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [doubleInl_comp h]
115	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
116	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) := relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x
117	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k)
118	          (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by rw [hx]
119	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (((Algebra.TensorProduct.map h h).restrictScalars k).comp
120	          (doubleInr E)) x := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x).symm
121	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((doubleInr F).comp (h.restrictScalars k)) x := by
122	        rw [doubleInr_comp h]
123	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr F) (relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k) x) :=
124	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ x

126	/-- Transport of descent classes along a refinement map of covers. -/
127	def descentMap {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
128	    descentClasses C E →* descentClasses C F :=
129	  ((relPicAlgMap C (h.restrictScalars k)).comp (descentClasses C E).subtype).codRestrict _
130	    fun x => relPicAlgMap_mem_descentClasses C h x.2

143	  rw [descentMap_coe,

147	lemma descentMap_comp {E F G : Algebra.EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
148	    (h' : F.Carrier →ₐ[A] G.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
149	    descentMap C (h'.comp h) x = descentMap C h' (descentMap C h x) := by
150	  ext
151	  rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe,
152	    show (h'.comp h).restrictScalars k
153	      = (h'.restrictScalars k).comp (h.restrictScalars k) from rfl]

156	/-- **Generalized refinement-map independence**, the keystone of the plus construction:
157	a class satisfying the descent condition restricts equally along any two `A`-algebra maps
158	out of the cover carrier — into an arbitrary test algebra, not merely another cover.  The
159	pair `(j₁, j₂)` factors jointly through the double cover of the source, where the descent
160	condition identifies the two pullbacks. -/
161	theorem relPicAlgMap_congr {E : Algebra.EtaleCover A} {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
162	    [Algebra k R] [Algebra A R] [IsScalarTower k A R] (j₁ j₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R)
163	    {x : relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)} (hx : x ∈ descentClasses C E) :
164	    relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by
165	  set H : E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier →ₐ[A] R :=
166	    Algebra.TensorProduct.lift j₁ j₂ fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _ with hH
167	  have key₁ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E) = j₁.restrictScalars k := by
168	    ext y
169	    simp [hH, doubleInl]
170	  have key₂ : (H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E) = j₂.restrictScalars k := by
171	    ext y
172	    simp [hH, doubleInr]
173	  calc relPicAlgMap C (j₁.restrictScalars k) x
174	      = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInl E)) x := by rw [key₁]
175	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInl E) x) :=
176	        relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
177	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (H.restrictScalars k) (relPicAlgMap C (doubleInr E) x) := by
178	        have hx' : relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInl E) x
179	            = relPicAlgMap (B := E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier) C (doubleInr E) x := hx
180	        rw [hx']
181	    _ = relPicAlgMap C ((H.restrictScalars k).comp (doubleInr E)) x :=
182	        (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
183	    _ = relPicAlgMap C (j₂.restrictScalars k) x := by rw [key₂]

185	/-- **Refinement-map independence**: any two refinement maps between the same covers
186	transport descent classes identically — what makes the plus construction independent of
187	all choices. -/
188	theorem descentMap_congr {E F : Algebra.EtaleCover A}
189	    (h₁ h₂ : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) (x : descentClasses C E) :
190	    descentMap C h₁ x = descentMap C h₂ x :=
191	  Subtype.ext (relPicAlgMap_congr C h₁ h₂ x.2)

193	/-! ## The plus construction -/
194	
195	/-- Two descent-class representatives are identified when they agree after transport to a
196	common refinement.  By `descentMap_congr` the choice of transport maps is immaterial, so
197	the relation is an equivalence (directedness of covers gives transitivity). -/
198	instance picEtAffSetoid : Setoid (Σ E : Algebra.EtaleCover A, descentClasses C E) where
199	  r p q := ∃ (F : Algebra.EtaleCover A) (f : p.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
200	    (g : q.1.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier), descentMap C f p.2 = descentMap C g q.2
201	  iseqv := by
202	    constructor
203	    · exact fun p => ⟨p.1, AlgHom.id A _, AlgHom.id A _, rfl⟩
204	    · rintro p q ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩
205	      exact ⟨F, g, f, hfg.symm⟩
206	    · rintro p q r ⟨F, f, g, hfg⟩ ⟨G, f', g', hfg'⟩
207	      refine ⟨F.prod G, (F.prodInl G).comp f, (F.prodInr G).comp g', ?_⟩
208	      rw [descentMap_comp, descentMap_comp, hfg, ← descentMap_comp, ← descentMap_comp,
209	        descentMap_congr C ((F.prodInl G).comp g) ((F.prodInr G).comp f') q.2,
210	        descentMap_comp, hfg', ← descentMap_comp]

363	/-- Every class pulled back from the base carries the tautological descent datum: the two
364	composites `A → B ⇉ B ⊗[A] B` coincide. -/
365	lemma tautological_mem_descentClasses (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
366	    (x : relPic C (overSpec k A)) :
367	    relPicAlgMap C ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k) x
368	      ∈ descentClasses C E := by
369	  rw [mem_descentClasses_iff, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp]
370	  congr 2
371	  ext a
372	  simp [doubleInl, doubleInr, Algebra.ofId_apply]

375	/-- The unit of the plus construction: a relative Picard class of the affine test,
376	pulled back to the trivial cover with its tautological descent datum. -/
377	def unit : relPic C (overSpec k A) →* PicEtAff C A where
378	  toFun x := mk C (.self A)
379	    ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
380	  map_one' := by
381	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) 1⟩ :
382	        descentClasses C (.self A)) = 1 from Subtype.ext (map_one _), mk_one]
383	  map_mul' x y := by
384	    rw [show (⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) (x * y)⟩ :
385	        descentClasses C (.self A))
386	        = ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) x⟩
387	          * ⟨_, tautological_mem_descentClasses C (.self A) y⟩ from
388	      Subtype.ext (map_mul _ x y), ← mk_mul_mk_same]
